items.title: One year after Dharali: The growing cost of building in a fragile Himalaya
items.summary: A year after the Dharali disaster, the reconstructed road leading to Gangotri has been shifted a few metres away from the banks of the Bhagirathi river. The market, once bustling with tourists during the yatra season, now wears a lifeless look. Most shops and houses still remain buried under debris. Apart from a handful of shops that have reopened, there is little sign of life. People are trying to piece together their lives, but they continue to face challenges. Dharali after the disaster of August 5, 2025. (Image courtesy Hridayesh Joshi) The disaster occurred in Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand on August 5 last year, after continuous rain on the almost vertical slopes caused a massive landslide in a village situated just about 20 kilometers from Gangotri. That day the Kheerganga, a tributary of the Bhagirathi, suddenly flooded and swept away a major part of Dharali – its market and homes. More than 50 people died and about 150 buildings were destroyed, including homes, hotels, and homestays. Newslaundry had extensively covered the disaster last year. Only one body was recovered in Dharali, and that too on the day of the disaster. “The relief workers were here only for a month.

Justice Bagchi warned that social media and algorithm-driven public outrage are reshaping how justice is perceived and social media was increasingly turning judicial proceedings into spectacles. items.summary: The Supreme Court recently quashed a cheating case against a man who was booked for riding a scooter with its rear number plate covered by a black mask [ Mohammed Abdul Ahad Shaker v. State of Telangana ]. In an order passed on July 28, a Bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih held that merely obstructing a vehicle's number plate would not constitute the offence of cheating under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) unless the essential ingredients of the offence are established. The Court clarified that covering the number plate of a vehicle could amount to a regulatory violation under the Motor Vehicles Act (MV Act) but such a violation could not be converted into a cheating offence. “ The regulatory breach of obstructing the number plate under the MV Act and rules thereunder cannot be dressed as an offence under Section 420 of the IPC without establishing the essential ingredients as required, ” the Court said. items.title: Lok Sabha passes Bill to increase Supreme Court judge strength to 38
items.summary: The Lok Sabha on Monday passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 by voice vote. The Bill raises the sanctioned judge strength of the Supreme Court from 33 to 38 (including the Chief Justice of India). It was moved by Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal. It amends Section 2 of the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956, substituting "thirty-seven" for "thirty-three." According to the Statement of Objects and Reasons of the Bill, the Supreme Court had 92,101 pending cases as on January 1, 2026. Despite operating at a near-full sanctioned strength of 34 judges since 2019, the Court recorded 75,410 new filings in 2025 against 65,615 disposals. The government cited this gap, along with the need for longer-sitting Constitution Benches, to seek the additional judges. The Bill's Financial Memorandum puts the recurring cost of the additional judges and their staff at about ₹10.57 crore a year, along with a one-time cost of about ₹3.47 crore for official residences and vehicles. items.title: Avoid terms like ‘helpless woman’ in rape judgments; no moral policing: Supreme Court panel to judges
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday released a report prepared by an expert committee headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice Aniruddha Bose , which made several recommendations to ensure a sensitive approach by judges who decide on cases involving sexual offences. Judges must avoid expressions such as “prosecutrix”, “helpless woman”, “lost her chastity” and “outraged her modesty” in judgments delivered in such cases, the report says. The report, titled Judgments and Gender: Sensitivity and Compassion in Writing Judgments , said that courts should instead use neutral and survivor-centric terms such as “victim”, “survivor”, “complainant”, “bodily autonomy” and “sexual assault." The committee prepared the recommendations after analysing 125 trial court judgments from across the country with the assistance of State judicial academies. It found a mixed picture concerning the sensitivity and approach of judges while dealing with victims, witnesses and vulnerable groups. The committee said sensitive judicial language was not merely a matter of politeness but was essential to ensuring fairness, dignity and impartiality in adjudication. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and the Indian Embassies in Ukraine and Romania to immediately take steps to ascertain the whereabouts of Indian seafarers aboard a cargo vessel that came under a drone attack near Ukraine. The Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana today noted that there were conflicting accounts emerging from the incident. Of the vessel's nine crew members, four were Indian. On report indicated that all four Indians had drowned. Another report indicated that two of the Indian seafarers were rescued at the scene, while the other two had to jump into the water to escape the fire and were currently with the Romanian Coast Guard. "We expect immediate steps from the Indian Embassy in Ukraine as well as in Romania to gather information about the whereabouts of these seafaring people. We also direct the Ministry of External Affairs to use their diplomatic channels and search in the same process," the Court said in its order today.
